title: Conjecture 1.6
statement_text: Given a partition of the vertex set of a path into sets $V_1, \ldots, V_m$ there exists an independent set $S$ and integers $b_i$, $i \leq m$, such that $|S \cap V_i| \geq \frac{|V_i|}{2} - b_i$ for all $i$, and 1. $\sum_{i \leq m} b_i \leq \frac{m}{2}$ and 2. $b_i \leq 1$ for all $i \leq m$.
context_text: The paper studies fair representation. For a simplicial complex $\mathcal{C}$ (a down-closed hypergraph, e.g. the independent sets of a graph, or the matchings of a graph, called its matching complex), $\beta(\mathcal{C})$ is the minimum number of members of $\mathcal{C}$ covering $V(\mathcal{C})$. A member $S$ represents a vertex set $A$ fairly if $|S\cap A|\ge\lfloor|A|/\beta(\mathcal{C})\rfloor$, and almost fairly if $|S\cap A|\ge\lfloor|A|/\beta(\mathcal{C})\rfloor-1$; the goal is to represent all parts of a partition of $V(\mathcal{C})$ (almost) fairly at once, like a parliament representing parties. This always works in matroids but not in general independence complexes. Matching complexes (independence complexes of line graphs) behave better: for every graph $H$ and partition $E_1,\dots,E_m$ of $E(H)$ there is a matching $M$ with $|M\cap E_i|\ge\lfloor|E_i|/(\Delta(L(H))+2)\rfloor$, where $L(H)$ is the line graph, a consequence of a topological connectivity bound for independence complexes of line graphs. For a path on $n$ vertices the independent sets have $\beta=2$, so fair representation means $|S\cap V_i|\ge|V_i|/2$ roughly; the matching complex of a path is the independence complex of a path one vertex shorter. The conjecture is a slightly stronger form of almost fair representation for paths: the total deficit $\sum b_i$ is at most $m/2$ and each individual deficit is at most 1. The authors prove each condition separately. Using the Borsuk–Ulam theorem, they get an independent set and integers $b_i$ with $\sum_i b_i\le m/2$ and $|S\cap V_i|\ge|V_i|/2-b_i$. Using Schrijver's strengthening of Lovász's Kneser theorem, they show that for every partition of the vertex set of a cycle into $V_1,\dots,V_m$ there is an independent set with $|S\cap V_i|\ge|V_i|/2-1$ for all $i$. Having both conditions at once is open. The conjecture is related to Ryser's conjecture on transversals of Latin squares.

title: Conjecture 1.9
statement_text: For any partition $E_1, E_2, \ldots, E_m$ of $E(K_{n,n})$ and any $j \leq m$ there exists a perfect matching $F$ in $K_{n,n}$ satisfying $|F \cap E_i| \geq \left\lfloor \frac{|E_i|}{n} \right\rfloor$ for all $i \neq j$, and $|F \cap E_j| \geq \left\lfloor \frac{|E_j|}{n} \right\rfloor - 1$.
context_text: The paper studies fair representation. For a simplicial complex $\mathcal{C}$ (a down-closed hypergraph, e.g. the independent sets of a graph, or the matchings of a graph, called its matching complex), $\beta(\mathcal{C})$ is the minimum number of members of $\mathcal{C}$ covering $V(\mathcal{C})$. A member $S$ represents a vertex set $A$ fairly if $|S\cap A|\ge\lfloor|A|/\beta(\mathcal{C})\rfloor$, and almost fairly if $|S\cap A|\ge\lfloor|A|/\beta(\mathcal{C})\rfloor-1$; the goal is to represent all parts of a partition of $V(\mathcal{C})$ (almost) fairly at once, like a parliament representing parties. This always works in matroids but not in general independence complexes. Matching complexes (independence complexes of line graphs) behave better: for every graph $H$ and partition $E_1,\dots,E_m$ of $E(H)$ there is a matching $M$ with $|M\cap E_i|\ge\lfloor|E_i|/(\Delta(L(H))+2)\rfloor$, where $L(H)$ is the line graph, a consequence of a topological connectivity bound for independence complexes of line graphs. For the matching complex of $K_{n,n}$, $\beta=n$ (the edges split into $n$ perfect matchings), so the conjecture says that any partition of $E(K_{n,n})$ is represented almost fairly by a perfect matching, with a deficit of at most one in a single prescribed class $E_j$ only. The authors prove it for $m=2$, where the main work is characterizing when a deficit is needed, and for $m=3$, by a topological argument using Sperner's lemma. A special case is the Stein-type conjecture that if $E(K_{n,n})$ is partitioned into $n$ sets of size $n$, some matching contains one edge from all but at most one set, related to the Brualdi–Stein conjecture on partial transversals of Latin squares. The paper's display has $\lfloor|E_i|/n\rfloor-1$ in the last inequality, an evident typo for $\lfloor|E_j|/n\rfloor-1$.

title: Conjecture 1.11 (Brualdi–Stein)
statement_text: If the edge set of $K_{n,n}$ is partitioned into sets $E_1, E_2, \ldots, E_n$ of size $n$ each, then there exists a matching in $K_{n,n}$ consisting of one edge from all but possibly one $E_i$.
context_text: Graph-theoretic reformulation of the Brualdi–Stein conjecture that every $n \times n$ Latin square has a partial transversal of size $n-1$, with Stein's observation that the Latin condition can be weakened to equal symbol distribution. Presented as a special case of the paper's Conjecture 1.9.
paper_contribution: Identifies this conjecture as a special case of the authors' Conjecture 1.9 for $m = n$, which is covered by Theorem 1.10 only for $m \leq 3$.

title: Conjecture 1.12
statement_text: If $E_1, E_2, \ldots, E_m$ are sets of edges in a bipartite graph, and $|E_i| > \Delta\!\left(\bigcup_{i \leq m} E_i\right) + 1$ then there exists a rainbow matching.
context_text: A related conjecture to Conjecture 1.9, suggested in reference [2] of the paper. The authors note one known example where $|E_i| \geq \Delta + 1$ does not suffice, and remark the conjecture is false when the $E_i$ are multisets.
paper_contribution: Discusses tightness of the bound and states a stronger generalisation as Conjecture 1.14; bibliography entry [2] not fully visible in extracted text.

title: Conjecture 1.14
statement_text: If the edge set of a graph $H$ is partitioned into sets $E_1, \ldots, E_m$ then there exists a matching $M$ satisfying $|M \cap E_i| \geq \left\lfloor \frac{|E_i|}{\Delta(H)+2} \right\rfloor$ for all $i \leq m$.
context_text: The paper studies fair representation. For a simplicial complex $\mathcal{C}$ (a down-closed hypergraph, e.g. the independent sets of a graph, or the matchings of a graph, called its matching complex), $\beta(\mathcal{C})$ is the minimum number of members of $\mathcal{C}$ covering $V(\mathcal{C})$. A member $S$ represents a vertex set $A$ fairly if $|S\cap A|\ge\lfloor|A|/\beta(\mathcal{C})\rfloor$, and almost fairly if $|S\cap A|\ge\lfloor|A|/\beta(\mathcal{C})\rfloor-1$; the goal is to represent all parts of a partition of $V(\mathcal{C})$ (almost) fairly at once, like a parliament representing parties. This always works in matroids but not in general independence complexes. Matching complexes (independence complexes of line graphs) behave better: for every graph $H$ and partition $E_1,\dots,E_m$ of $E(H)$ there is a matching $M$ with $|M\cap E_i|\ge\lfloor|E_i|/(\Delta(L(H))+2)\rfloor$, where $L(H)$ is the line graph, a consequence of a topological connectivity bound for independence complexes of line graphs. $\Delta(H)$ is the maximum degree of $H$. The conjecture is a stronger version of a conjecture of Aharoni, Barát and Wanless on rainbow matchings: if $E_1,\dots,E_m$ are sets of edges of a bipartite graph with $|E_i|>\Delta(\bigcup_i E_i)+1$ for all $i$, then there is a rainbow matching (one edge from each $E_i$, pairwise disjoint). There is an example where $|E_i|\ge\Delta+1$ does not suffice, and that conjecture fails for multisets. The bound $\Delta(H)+2$ mirrors the connectivity bound for independence complexes of line graphs, which gives the weaker known result above with $\Delta(L(H))+2$ in place of $\Delta(H)+2$.

title: Conjecture 1.15
statement_text: For every $m$ there exists a number $c(m)$ for which the following is true: if $G$ is a bipartite graph and $E_1, \ldots, E_m$ are any sets of edges, then there exists a matching $S$ in $G$ of size at least $\frac{|E(G)|}{\Delta(G)} - c(m)$ such that $|S \cap E_i| \leq \left\lceil \frac{|E_i|}{\Delta(G)} \right\rceil$ for all $i \leq m$.
context_text: The paper studies fair representation. For a simplicial complex $\mathcal{C}$ (a down-closed hypergraph, e.g. the independent sets of a graph, or the matchings of a graph, called its matching complex), $\beta(\mathcal{C})$ is the minimum number of members of $\mathcal{C}$ covering $V(\mathcal{C})$. A member $S$ represents a vertex set $A$ fairly if $|S\cap A|\ge\lfloor|A|/\beta(\mathcal{C})\rfloor$, and almost fairly if $|S\cap A|\ge\lfloor|A|/\beta(\mathcal{C})\rfloor-1$; the goal is to represent all parts of a partition of $V(\mathcal{C})$ (almost) fairly at once, like a parliament representing parties. This always works in matroids but not in general independence complexes. Matching complexes (independence complexes of line graphs) behave better: for every graph $H$ and partition $E_1,\dots,E_m$ of $E(H)$ there is a matching $M$ with $|M\cap E_i|\ge\lfloor|E_i|/(\Delta(L(H))+2)\rfloor$, where $L(H)$ is the line graph, a consequence of a topological connectivity bound for independence complexes of line graphs. $\Delta(G)$ is the maximum degree of $G$; by König's theorem the edges of a bipartite graph $G$ split into $\Delta(G)$ matchings, so a matching of size about $|E(G)|/\Delta(G)$ is a natural target. Over-representation statements like the conjectures above easily fail when the sets $E_i$ are not a partition, which suggests stating them as under-representation by a large matching. When the $E_i$ form a partition, the under-representation condition implies that all but $c(m)$ sets are fairly represented, and it defines a generalized partition matroid, so the conjecture concerns representation by a set in the intersection of three matroids. The authors suggest that $c(m)=m/2$ may suffice.
